descriptors.concept_name: Deduction At Source And Advance Payment [Section 190]
descriptors.definition: Income tax is primarily taxable in the assessment year following the previous year, but collection occurs within the previous year through tax deduction at source, tax collection at source, and advance tax payments. These collected amounts are deductible from the total tax liability determined when filing the return of income.
inclusion: TDS
TCS
Advance tax
exclusion: Post-assessment recovery proceedings initiated without prior collection mechanisms
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard retrospective year-end tax payment by shifting collection obligations into the earning period.

descriptors.definition: Assessees must pay tax directly when income is not subject to statutory tax deduction at source or when liable tax is not actually deducted by the deductor. Failure by a deductor to pay withheld or required taxes results in being deemed an assessee-in-default, unless the underlying tax is paid directly by the assessee.
inclusion: Direct payments on non-deducted incomes
Deferred tax payments on specified securities or sweat equity shares from eligible start-ups
exclusion: Incomes where proper statutory TDS is successfully executed and remitted by the deductor
nearby_distinctions: Differs from routine TDS where a third party withholds tax; direct payment places the immediate remittance burden back on the income recipient or penalized deductor.

descriptors.definition: Employers responsible for salary payouts must calculate and deduct income tax at the time of payment based on the employee's estimated total income and selected tax regime. If an employee fails to intimate their tax regime preference, tax must be computed using the default statutory tax rates.
inclusion: Salary disbursements
Estimated total income calculations utilizing default or opted tax structures
exclusion: Non-salary compensatory streams governed by separate specific TDS sections
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from other collection mechanisms due to its mandatory linkage to the timing of actual salary payments rather than mere accrual.

descriptors.definition: Every person responsible for disbursing salary income is legally obligated to deduct income tax at the time of payment using the applicable average tax rate. Deductors must collect tax regime intentions from employees to correctly apply default or opted tax configurations.
inclusion: Payments chargeable under the head Salaries
exclusion: Income categories falling outside employment remuneration
nearby_distinctions: Applies strictly to employer-employee remuneration payouts unlike contract or professional fee deductions.

descriptors.concept_name: Premature withdrawal from Employees Provident Fund [Section 192A]
descriptors.definition: Premature withdrawals from recognized provident funds before five years of continuous service are subject to tax and require tax deduction at source. Trustees calculate this tax liability by recomputing historical contributions as if directed to an unrecognized provident fund.
instrument_references: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act 1952
inclusion: Withdrawals made prior to five continuous years of service without approved balances transfer
exclusion: Withdrawals after continuous service of five years or due to exempt conditions like ill health or business discontinuance
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard salary TDS by focusing on accumulated provident fund corpus adjustments rather than periodic periodic employment earnings.

descriptors.definition: Any person paying interest on securities to a resident must deduct income tax at the specified rates upon credit or payment, whichever occurs earlier. Specific government bonds, loans, and notified public sector debentures are exempted from these deduction requirements.
inclusion: Interest on Central or State Government securities
Interest on debentures issued by companies or local authorities
exclusion: Notified National Defence bonds, loans, and specific capital gains bonds
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general bank or corporate interest by applying specifically to formal monetary securities and debentures.

descriptors.definition: The principal officer of a domestic company must deduct tax when distributing or paying dividends to resident shareholders. Specific small-value non-cash distributions to individuals and payouts to institutional insurers or specialized IFSC aircraft leasing units are exempt.
inclusion: Actual dividend distributions
Amounts deemed as dividend under statutory provisions
exclusion: Non-cash dividend payments to individuals not exceeding the threshold limit
Distributions to qualifying institutional insurers and notified IFSC units
nearby_distinctions: Restricts tax withholding obligations exclusively to resident shareholders as opposed to foreign recipients.

descriptors.concept_name: Interest other than interest on securities [Section 194A]
descriptors.definition: Non-individual assessees, along with large business individuals or HUFs exceeding specific turnover limits, must deduct tax at source on non-security interest paid to residents. Automated core banking software provisioning for macro-monitoring does not constitute constructive credit triggering immediate TDS obligations.
inclusion: Interest payments from non-exempt entities to resident payees
Periodic or maturity-based interest credits on bank time deposits
exclusion: Routine daily or monthly macro-monitoring provisioning entries lacking constructive credit in core banking systems
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from interest on securities by excluding formal debentures and government security yields in favor of general bank and commercial interest.

descriptors.concept_name: Winnings from lotteries, crossword puzzles, etc. and horse races [Sections 194B and 194BB]
descriptors.definition: Payer entities must deduct tax at a flat rate of thirty percent on winnings from lotteries, card games, betting, or horse races exceeding statutory thresholds. When winnings are provided partly or wholly in kind without sufficient cash cover, tax must be verified as paid prior to release.
inclusion: Lottery prizes
Card game and gambling winnings
Horse race payouts through licensed bookmakers
exclusion: Winnings sourced from online games governed by distinct regulatory frameworks
nearby_distinctions: Separated from online gaming winnings by applying strictly to traditional physical lotteries, betting, and real-world racecourse events.

descriptors.definition: Entities responsible for paying online gaming winnings must deduct tax at source on net winnings calculated within user accounts at the end of the financial year or upon withdrawal. If payouts include non-cash items lacking sufficient cash balances to cover liabilities, tax payment verification is mandatory prior to release.
inclusion: Net winnings withdrawn from user accounts
Year-end net balances inside digital gaming user accounts
exclusion: Traditional physical lotteries and racecourse betting winnings
nearby_distinctions: Differs from conventional physical betting rules by focusing on algorithmic net winnings inside internet-accessible digital user accounts.

descriptors.definition: Specified entities and large business operators making payments to resident contractors for carrying out any work must deduct tax at source upon credit or payment. Payments made by individuals or HUFs exclusively for personal purposes are exempt from these withholding obligations.
inclusion: Contract sums for labor and construction work
Payments made by qualified businesses, governments, and large enterprises
exclusion: Payments made by individuals or HUFs strictly for non-business personal purposes
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from professional fees by applying explicitly to contractual execution of work rather than specialized professional services.

descriptors.definition: Entities paying remuneration or commission to resident agents for soliciting or procuring insurance business must deduct tax at source when payments exceed statutory financial year limits. Non-compliant sums received under life insurance policies lacking exemption are similarly subjected to specific withholding rates.
inclusion: Insurance solicitation commissions
Taxable payouts from non-exempt life insurance policies
exclusion: Exempt insurance proceeds fully compliant with statutory conditions
nearby_distinctions: Targets insurance remuneration specifically, separating it from standard commercial contract payments and brokerage fees.
